title: Supernova Simulation: an interactive browser-based model of stellar death, from core collapse to the view from Earth
description:
An interactive, physically-motivated simulation of how stars die, running entirely in the browser. Users pick a real star (Betelgeuse, Antares, Rigel, Spica, VY Canis Majoris, Eta Carinae, Sirius A, Vega, the Sun, Proxima Centauri) or build their own, fast-forward its evolution, watch the core collapse and the ejecta expand in a WebGL scene at true relative scale, and then step outside to see what the explosion looks like from Earth, including the light travel time, the apparent magnitude on a panoramic night sky, and order-of-magnitude estimates of ozone depletion, UV-B increase, cosmic-ray flux and neutrino dose.

The supernova model is analytic: core collapse, bounce, shock breakout, a Popov (1993) plateau, a radioactive 56Ni/56Co tail (Nadyozhin 1994), free expansion and a Sedov–Taylor phase. Remnants (white dwarf, neutron star, pulsar, magnetar, black hole, or none) follow simplified literature prescriptions. Every value in the interface is labelled Observed, Estimated or Simulation. The software is intended for education and outreach; it is not a hydrodynamics code and makes no predictions about when any real star will explode.

Built with Three.js and Vite. No backend, textures, datasets or API keys are required; the built site is under 1 MB.
notes: Educational model. All numerical outputs are approximations; see the README sections 'Simulation limitations' and 'Scientific approximations'.
